- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias toward lower prices.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% in 30d), model often overshoots and forecasts higher than true — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent mean.
- Model frequently underpredicts mean reversion in 30d horizon — if 18d history shows volatility, forecast should be slightly above 18d average to capture reversion bias.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment history contains multiple 0.00 entries (neutral), model tends to overestimate volatility — dampen forecast variance by 10–20% in 30d horizon.
